rationale: bugs_open/337: component-creator/generate_template is capped at ai_service.max_tokens=16000 and one section type (loans-credit-health-check) deterministically needs more — nine truncations 08-15..08-19, every one cut at output_tokens=16000 with 46,441-48,817 chars recovered, three work items each burning three full-price generations before parking failed, two live loan-site pages shipped hollow. The retries are spent on a deterministic refusal (016b §9 entry of 2026-08-20, filed from this bug). Two measured facts widen it beyond one section: (1) the cap is tight for the step's ORDINARY work — successful calls' p95 is 13,633 of 16,000 (85%), max 15,374 (96%); (2) the fleet headroom monitor LCO-007 has flagged exactly this step since 08-18 (T generate_template@16000, truncated 9) and nothing consumed the flag. The estate's recorded doctrine (aiservice/truncation.go:26-29; bugs 019/183/119) is that raising a cap alone moves the cliff, so this change ships the pair: a FRAMEWORK seam — an opt-in ai_service.max_tokens_ceiling key giving execute_llm_prompt ONE in-call retry at the ceiling when the typed TruncatedError fires and the ceiling strictly exceeds the wire cap the cut call was sent with — plus a measured resize of this step (16000->24000 routine, 32000 ceiling) via migration 549. The seam is the honest narrow form of the bug file's candidate 3: not a continuation call, not a fleet default, no change for the 67 execute_llm_prompt carriers that do not name the key (owner ruling 2026-08-02 §2 opt-in shape, the same shape MDL-041 shipped into this seam). It is deliberately distinct from the bugs_closed/119 re-ask, which refuses to raise the cap because it serves a judgement that can be re-asked shorter — a 47k-char component document cannot be asked shorter, its length IS the work product, so the only honest retry for a writer step is a taller bounded one. tolerate_truncation is wrong here on the record (012/205: a whole-component writer must never persist a fragment; the 076 guard would rightly refuse it). Sizing is from measurement, not taste: 24000 clears the ordinary p95 by ~75% and the failing section's extrapolated 19-22k need; 32000 is the largest CLOCK-SAFE ceiling (step measures 92-127 tok/s on sonnet-4-6 against the non-streaming 600s timeout; 40k+ at a conservative 60 tok/s crosses the timeout and converts a loud truncation into a silent clock death, the strictly worse trade per LCO-007's C-vs-T doctrine). Routine deliberately != ceiling so demand above 24000 stays a countable forensic event (the ESCALATED llm_call_log row) rather than invisible headroom erosion. Reuse note: no existing mechanism does this — the 119 re-ask is parse-failure-scoped and cap-preserving; tolerate_truncation salvages fragments; MDL-041's per-call options[max_tokens] precedence (rule 1, wins at the wire) is exactly what lets this escalation work with ZERO provider-client changes. Registered as MDL-042 in the same commit (ordering-exemption condition 2). Consumers told: recorded in bugs_open/337 + register naming diagnose-agent/verdict@32000 and tool-improver/improve_tool@32000 as the visible next candidates, their owners' call.

plan.summary: generate_template deterministically exceeds its 16,000-token output cap for one section type and burns 3 full generations per item before parking pages hollow. Add an opt-in escalate-on-truncation seam to execute_llm_prompt (ai_service.max_tokens_ceiling: one in-call retry at the ceiling on a typed TruncatedError, cut call logged ESCALATED), and resize the step from measurement via migration 549 (24000 routine + 32000 ceiling, 415-pattern resolved-value asserts). Steps without the key run byte-identically.

edits.rationale: The whole escalation decision as a pure function so it is testable without a provider client (createAIClient has no seam). Accepts int/int64/float64/json.Number for the ceiling because the same key arrives as float64 from jsonb and int from viper YAML — the exact defect max_tokens.go documents on ai_actions.go:361. Refuses ceiling <= sentMaxTokens: an identical-height retry on a deterministic cut is the measured waste (nine cap-hits, zero successes), and refusal keeps a misconfiguration inert instead of silently doubling spend.

The decision table IS the behaviour: escalates on typed (and %w-wrapped) truncation with a taller ceiling, including over the 2048 provider fallback; refuses on no-key (the opt-in contract — byte-identical old path), ceiling <= sent, non-truncation errors (a 529 retried taller is just a more expensive 529), nil error, zero/negative/string ceilings. Second test pins all four numeric arrival types so the YAML-int case cannot silently drop.

Wiring, placed BETWEEN the GenerateText call and the existing error block so that block only ever sees the FINAL attempt's error — a truncation at the ceiling, a 5xx, anything, flows through tolerate_truncation (with its 076 guard), isAIUnavailable, the transient ladder and the catch-all verbatim, with no second error path to drift. The cut first call gets its own llm_call_log row (one call, one forensic row — the package rule), prefixed ESCALATED so a census counts escalations without joins. Options-map mutation between the two calls is safe: LogLLMCall reads the map synchronously before its goroutine (llm_call_logger.go:35-39, the comment says exactly this). llmCallStart is reset so each row carries its own latency. On escalated success, execution falls through to the existing success path, which logs the second call's row with the ceiling as max_tokens — headroom queries then see the escalated call at its real cap.

The resize half, live on apply: 16000->24000 routine + max_tokens_ceiling 32000 in one statement. Follows migration 415 (assert the RESOLVED value in the resolver's precedence order, never the key just written — the 413 trap; refuse if a top-level max_tokens outranks the step key) and 484 (snapshot_agent first; pre-state gate IS DISTINCT FROM '16000' refusing to overwrite a concurrent change; double-apply refusal on the ceiling; negative control that the inert config.max_tokens spelling was not minted). The ceiling key is INERT until the chassis roll — staged arming stated in the file header; no ordering constraint either direction. Rollback sidecar 549_..._ROLLBACK.sql restores 16000 and removes the ceiling. 067-sweep note: generate_template is component-creator's only execute_llm_prompt step, so this is the whole sweep for the agent.

plan.risks: The transient 5xx ladder inside the error block now retries at the ceiling if the escalated call draws a 5xx (bounded by the operator's own ceiling; deliberate, no second path). A truncation AT the ceiling still burns the work item's remaining attempts identically — named residual, belongs to the RSH-007/WII failure-ladder contract, not smuggled in here. The ceiling key is inert until the chassis rolls: a session reading live config before the roll may mistake it for dead config — the migration header, MDL-042 and bugs_open/337 all state the staged arming. The migration refuses to apply if the live cap is no longer exactly 16000 (a concurrent change aborts it harmlessly — re-derive against the live value). execute_vision_prompt does not escalate (stated in MDL-042). Reviewers should check: (1) the wiring really does precede every consumer of the first call's error so no stale isTruncatedCall/truncErr survives an escalated success — the escalation block recomputes nothing and the existing block re-derives everything from the final err; (2) the ESCALATED row cannot double-count in per-step success-rate queries (it is success=false, same as the pre-change single row; failures filtered on success=false are unchanged in count only when escalation is off — an opted-in step that escalates-and-succeeds shows one failed + one successful row, which is the honest record of two calls).
